title: Henry Therian, Joe Virgis and writing Too Late to Be Sorry Now
summary: Leclerc, Joe Virgis and Texas singer Henri Therian wrote Too Late to Be Sorry Now; all three names are on the Cameo record.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. I wrote another song, Why Should I Believe in You? Yeah, but I never do much on it. It was published.
Therian? He was from Texas. He was a singer.
His first name? I don't remember. Henry Therian.
And he was from out in Texas. You know what part of Texas? No, I really don't know.

Was he in town or something? How'd you meet him? It's possible that he sang because he had a marvelous voice. It's possible that he sang one of the places and that's where we met him. Joe Voyage just met him. And then the three of us got together and we wrote Too Late to Be Sorry Now. I think he wrote the lyrics. I think Joe and I fooled around and played the melody. We got the melody.
Well, on this record it has Therian's name.
Yeah. The one by... Henry Therian, yeah. Isn't it gonna say Henry?
Yeah. H-E-N-R-I. That's why he spelled his name in those days.
Yeah, well this is a cameo number 460 by Fred Shaw.
Well, what other name do they have?
Yeah, three. That was correct. Oh, yeah. Yeah, Henry Therian and myself and Joe.
